PROBE (scratchpad subname.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl at a6b2a574): `my $s = set_subname("main::x\x00y", sub { (caller(0))[3] })` -- perl: subname($s) = `main::x` (perl TRUNCATES the name at the NUL in subname's answer? no: it is the stash name up to the NUL as the test expects), $s->() = `main::x\x00y`; PCL: subname = `__ANON__`, $s->() = `` (EMPTY).  The PLAIN name fails the same way: `set_subname("Foo::plain", sub { (caller(0))[3] })` -> perl `Foo::plain / Foo::plain`, PCL `__ANON__ / ` -- so set_subname does nothing in lib/Sub/Util.pm (line 61) and `caller(0)[3]` inside an ANON sub answers empty where perl answers `main::__ANON__`.  TWO mechanisms, same file: (1) the shim's set_subname must RENAME the function (the s521d #3492 named-lambda carries `PKG::__ANON__`; a rename = a new name on that record + subname reading it) and `subname` must read it back; (2) caller(0)[3] for an anon sub = `PKG::__ANON__` (perl) -- today empty; after set_subname = the set name.  The `natively compiled sub` half (string-eval'd `sub NAME {...}` with exotic bytes in NAME, then `(caller(0))[3]` + the stash key) tests the same two answers for a NAMED sub with NUL / control / high bytes in its name.  Rows: bless the 908 with THIS cause (done s523 round 3); acceptance = `tools/run-dist-t.pl --rows --no-dist-lib ~/.cpan/build/Scalar-List-Utils-1.70-0 t/exotic_names.t` 652/908 -> 1560/0; also subname.t (21 rows, ruled XS) may move.
